purpose: Measure whether Brali's trusted and problem-first surfaces are gaining useful search discovery before expanding the indexable corpus again.
baseline_gate: Do not use raw sitemap size as a growth target and do not start another broad promotion/index-policy wave until a real Search Console baseline has been captured under this segmentation.

segments.label: Trusted current guidance
segments.definition: Canonical /life-os/ protocol records present in the reviewed/practical Protocol Feed.

segments.label: Problem and question discovery
segments.definition: Curated /problems/ and /questions/ surfaces that map human intent to Brali knowledge.

segments.label: Research, data and AI
segments.definition: Research, For-AI, API, dataset, agent, skill and benchmark surfaces intended for evidence inspection or machine reuse.

segments.label: Review-required neutral records
segments.definition: Other /life-os/<slug>/ records that are not in the current trusted Protocol Feed. Search discovery does not make them recommendable.

segments.label: Legacy and archive surfaces
segments.definition: Compatibility, archived, or explicitly legacy discovery surfaces.

segments.label: Other indexable surfaces
segments.definition: Pages that do not fit a maintained Brali measurement segment yet; inspect before assigning conclusions.

opportunity_rules.rule: Rank high-impression queries from the Search Console top-query sample that do not resolve to a canonical Problem Discovery Graph entry. Treat them as review/prioritization input, not proof that a new page should be created.

interpretation_limits: Search Console top page and top query arrays are samples from the configured row limit, not complete zero-filled inventories.
Clicks, impressions, CTR and average position are observational search metrics and do not prove that a repository change caused a ranking movement.
An indexed review-required record remains non-recommendable until its evidence state changes through Brali's review workflow.
A query with impressions is a demand signal, not permission to generate a thin keyword page or weaken evidence gates.
Segment comparisons should be repeated over time with the same definitions before making index-policy decisions.
